title: Sequence analysis of LipL41 and LipL21: Prospective Outer Membrane Proteins (OMPs) in early diagnosing leptospirosis
author: Mosquill, Nordin, et al.

steps.title: Identify conserved OMP sequences
steps.instruction: Download the protein sequences of LipL21, LipL31, LipL41 and LipL46 from the NCBI database, align them with MUSCLE, view the alignment in Jalview, calculate percent identity and locate conserved regions; select LipL21 (conserved in intermediate Leptospira) and LipL41 (conserved in pathogenic Leptospira) as the target genes for primer design.

steps.title: Design primers from conserved regions
steps.instruction: Use NCBI Primer‑Blast to design PCR primers based on the conserved sequences of LipL21 and LipL41. Record the primer sequences listed in Table 1: LipL21 forward ATG GTC TTT CGA AGG CTG GGGTT GCT TCA CCG TCG GAA AC (258 bp amplicon) and LipL41 forward CGT AAC GTA GGT TTG GCT GTTGC TTC GTT GAT TGC GTC TG (174 bp amplicon); reverse primers are as listed in Table 1.

steps.title: Culture Leptospira and extract DNA
steps.instruction: Grow the selected Leptospira species (including L. biflexa serovar Patoc, L. licerasiae serovar Varillal, L. fainei serovar Hurstbridge, L. interrogans serovar Icterohaemorrhagiae, L. weilii serovar Caledonia) in EMJH medium, monitor growth by dark‑field microscopy, extract genomic DNA with the Nucleospin Tissue DNA extraction kit (Macherey‑Nagel, Germany), quantify DNA on a Nanodrop spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and dilute each extract to 10 µg/mL with RNase‑free deionized water.

steps.title: Optimize annealing temperature (gradient PCR)
steps.instruction: For each primer set, prepare eight 25 µL PCR reactions using exTEN 2X PCR Master Mix (1st Base, Singapore) as follows per reaction: 12.5 µL Master Mix, 1.5 µL forward primer (10 µM), 1.5 µL reverse primer (10 µM), 7.5 µL RNase‑free water, 2 µL DNA template (L. fainei serovar Hurstbridge for LipL21; L. interrogans serovar Icterohaemorrhagiae for LipL41). Dispense equally into tubes A–H (≈25 µL each). Run on a Bio‑Rad CFX96 thermal cycler with the program: 95 °C 60 s initial activation; 35 cycles of 95 °C 15 s denaturation, annealing at a gradient of 50‑60 °C for 30 s (temperatures per tube: A 60.0 °C, B 59.4 °C, C 58.3 °C, D 56.3 °C, E 53.9 °C, F 52.0 °C, G 50.7 °C, H 50.0 °C), 72 °C 60 s extension; final extension 72 °C 600 s. After amplification, run the products on agarose gel to identify the temperature giving the strongest specific band.

steps.title: Prepare 1.8 % agarose gel and run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Mix 1.8 g agarose powder with 100 mL 1X TAE buffer (Thermo Scientific, Lithuania), melt in a microwave for 2–3 min, let cool to ~50 °C, add 1 µL EtB”Out” nucleic‑acid staining solution (Yeastern Biotech, Taiwan), pour into a gel tray with combs and allow to solidify. Place the gel in an electrophoresis tank containing 1X TAE, orient wells toward the negative electrode, load 5 µL 100 bp DNA ladder (Excelband, Taiwan) into the first well and 5 µL of each PCR product into subsequent wells. Run at 100 V for 45 min, then visualize bands with a Bio‑Rad GelDoc Go imaging system.

steps.title: Perform singleplex PCR assay
steps.instruction: Using the annealing temperature determined to be optimal (52.0 °C), set up PCR reactions for each primer set with the same master‑mix composition as the gradient experiment. Include: positive controls – LipL21: DNA from L. fainei serovar Hurstbridge; LipL41: DNA from L. interrogans serovar Icterohaemorrhagiae; negative control – RNase‑free water; test samples – DNA from L. biflexa serovar Patoc (saprophytic), L. licerasiae serovar Varillal (intermediate) for LipL21, L. fainei serovar Hurstbridge (intermediate) for LipL41, and L. weilii serovar Caledonia (pathogenic). Run PCR with the program described in step 4 (fixed annealing at 52.0 °C). Resolve the amplified products on a 1.8 % agarose gel (100 V, 45 min) and image as in step 5.
